method: All 198 original source coordinates, face IDs, directions, and ray lengths retained. The endpoint is source+original_direction*original_length. Shared exact raw STL vertices and recomputed outward face-normal angle quantify adjacency. For each original chord midpoint, +/- coordinate-axis first-boundary rays quantify connected local solid chords. Fixed XY/XZ/YZ sections go through the unaltered original source coordinate (no offset/resampling); contours use the original check_layers.py 1e-4 mm endpoint-clustering/degree-two/even-odd algorithm. Sections clipped to 0.8/1.6/3.2mm squares and exact-solid Boolean intersections with 1.6/3.2mm cubes give nearby material, with no warning suppressed.
limitations: Axis chords are material intervals through the original normal-chord midpoint, not a global wall-thickness proof.

Fixed source planes can coincide with original planar faces: closed=false is retained as an unresolved sectional numerical degeneracy; independent local 3D cube intersections still quantify original nearby solid.
Local Boolean volume uses double-precision Manifold from original float32 STL, not exact rational CSG or a slicer.
Classification distinguishes manufacture-relevant protrusions from ray boundary artifacts but does not confer print approval. No slicing or print was performed.
